climate.overview_html: Reaction to COP31's collapse continued: Panama rejected the outcome and the presidency declared the Antalya Pact not adopted. Voluntary tracks such as the electrification package survive. The fight over the IPCC report timeline moves to a December session.

items.headline: Panama rejects COP31 outcome as civil society calls the summit a failure
items.summary: COP31 President Murat Kurum declared the Antalya Pact not adopted. Oxfam said the summit delivered no meaningful outcomes, Canada called the result not what it hoped, and co-president Australia faced criticism at home.

items.headline: COP31 hosts back a voluntary electrification package
items.summary: The COP31 Electrification Delivery Package groups pledges to replace direct fossil fuel use with electric alternatives. It sat outside the negotiated text, so it stands despite the failed cover decision.

items.headline: IPCC report timeline dispute heads to a December session
items.summary: Saudi Arabia, China and India want the seventh assessment reports delayed to 2029, after the 2028 global stocktake. The IPCC suspended its last session over the dispute and hopes to settle the timeline in December.

items.headline: Pacific Islands present 70 renewable projects worth $2.3bn at COP31
items.summary: Pacific governments pitched a pipeline of 70 renewable energy projects valued at US$2.3 billion to investors and donors at the summit.

major_events.name: Thanksgiving coastal storm, eastern US
major_events.impact: A coastal low brings rain, gusts of 35-50 mph and minor to moderate coastal flooding from the mid-Atlantic to New England on Thanksgiving, with possible major flooding just north of Norfolk, Virginia. Rain totals of 1-3 inches are forecast in Virginia. Weather.com puts the chance of Macy's parade balloons being grounded at about 40%.

major_events.name: Pacific storm series, US West Coast
major_events.impact: AccuWeather expects at least three more storms before Thanksgiving. The strongest arrives Tuesday into Wednesday with winds that could down trees and cut power, coinciding with king tides; snow levels will be higher than in earlier storms.

major_events.name: Central Florida river flooding
major_events.status: St. Johns at Sanford heading to major
major_events.impact: The state emergency covers 21 counties after more than 100 water rescues in Brevard County. NWS Melbourne expects the St. Johns River at Sanford to reach major flood stage around midweek; downstream at Cocoa the river is already above its 1953 record.

major_events.name: Southern Thailand and Malaysia monsoon floods
major_events.impact: Thailand's Hydro-Informatics Institute warned all 11 Phatthalung districts of flash floods and hill runoff on saturated ground. Malaysia's NADMA reported floods and landslides in Selangor, Perak, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka last week.

major_events.name: Kimberley heatwave, Western Australia
major_events.status: Extreme, easing to severe by Wed
major_events.impact: Extreme heatwave conditions are developing across the Kimberley on Nov 23-24 before easing to severe by Wednesday, with a severe heatwave warning also in place for the North Interior. Severe storms are forecast across eastern Australia through Friday.

major_events.name: Early cold in UK and Italy
major_events.impact: A Scandinavian air mass brings frost, sub-zero nights and snow on Scottish hills and the Pennines this week; a yellow cold health alert covers parts of northern England. Arctic air is also driving a deep low over Italy, with snow to low elevations on Wednesday.

weather.overview_html: A coastal storm brings rain, 35-50 mph gusts and coastal flooding to the US East Coast on Thanksgiving, while Pacific storms hit the West Coast. In Florida the St. Johns River at Sanford is heading for major flood stage. Monsoon rain keeps southern Thailand and Malaysia on flood alert.

items.headline: Thanksgiving storm to bring rain, wind and coastal flooding from Virginia to New England
items.summary: Thursday is the peak day across much of the Northeast, and the storm moves through quickly rather than stalling. Numerous coastal locations face minor to moderate flooding, with major flooding possible just north of Norfolk.

items.headline: Widespread rain set for Thanksgiving in northeast Ohio
items.summary: The station issued a First Alert Day for rain and blustery conditions on Thursday, with highs in the 40s. Inland impacts are milder than on the coast.

items.headline: At least three more Pacific storms to hit the West Coast before Thanksgiving
items.summary: The strongest arrives Tuesday into Wednesday with winds that could down trees and cut power. King tides Tuesday through Thursday coincide with its landfall.

items.headline: St. Johns River at Sanford forecast to reach major flood stage midweek
items.summary: Levels at Sanford are rising through moderate flood stage in Seminole County. The warning follows a 21-county state emergency and Melbourne's wettest November on record, with more than 17 inches of rain.

items.headline: Thailand warns all 11 Phatthalung districts of flash floods on Nov 23-25
items.summary: The Hydro-Informatics Institute cited rain on already saturated ground. Officials are watching four canals and runoff from the Banthat mountains.

items.headline: Floods and landslides hit five Malaysian states as monsoon rain spreads
items.summary: The ASEAN disaster centre's weekly update lists floods in Selangor, Perak, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka, plus heavy-rain flooding in Indonesia and southern Thailand. No tropical cyclone was active in the ASEAN region.

items.headline: Extreme heatwave develops across the Kimberley
items.summary: Conditions reach extreme on Nov 23-24 before easing to severe by Wednesday. A severe heatwave warning remains for the North Interior.

items.headline: UK issues yellow cold health alert as Met Office forecasts early winter
items.summary: The alert covers parts of northern England. London could fall to 0C this week, with snow on Scottish hills and the Pennines and widespread frost.

renewables.overview_html: NERC's winter assessment says about 9 GW of new batteries helped cut US elevated-risk areas from seven to three, though gas supply in a long cold snap remains the weak point. India lost 8,133 GWh of solar to curtailment in one quarter, and Madhya Pradesh approved an 800 MW battery beside its floating solar.

items.headline: NERC cuts winter elevated-risk areas to three as batteries and gas add 26 GW
items.summary: NERC's 2026-27 winter assessment credits about 9 GW each of new batteries and gas, against peak demand 21 GW higher than last winter. Gas supply in a long, wide cold snap remains the main risk, and El Niño shapes the regional outlook.

items.headline: India's solar curtailment reached 8,133 GWh in April-June
items.summary: A YES Securities report says grid constraints hit hardest in Rajasthan and Gujarat and may slow solar capacity growth after FY28.

items.headline: Madhya Pradesh approves 200 MW floating solar and 800 MW battery at Omkareshwar
items.summary: The state cabinet's approval brings planned floating solar on the Omkareshwar reservoir to 478 MW. The battery would let the plant shift output beyond daylight hours.

items.headline: Lebanon plans 3-3.5 GW of new capacity led by solar, wind and storage
items.summary: The cabinet approved the plan, and the government is exploring cooperation with Qatar on renewable and storage projects.

items.headline: October irradiance ran over 20% above average in Southeast Asia
items.summary: Solcast attributes the gains in southern China and Southeast Asia to strong El Niño conditions, persistent high pressure and less cloud. Sichuan came in below average.

items.headline: Philippines signs offshore wind agreement with China's Ming Yang
items.summary: President Marcos signed the agreement to build out offshore wind infrastructure and cut reliance on imported fuel.

science.overview_html: Two tropical cyclone studies stand out: an AGU paper finds typhoons crossing marine heatwaves are up to three times likelier to rapidly intensify, and a UAlbany test of Google's cyclone model flags weaknesses on the strongest storms. MIT researchers showed a way to keep AI emulators of chaotic systems bounded, and WeatherCraft reports a 17.6% day-15 error cut.

items.headline: MIT method keeps AI models of chaotic systems physically bounded
items.summary: Researchers built physical constraints into machine-learning models of chaotic systems so predictions cannot run away to impossible values. Tests used standard benchmark systems, not operational weather or climate forecasts.

items.headline: Typhoons over marine heatwaves are up to three times likelier to rapidly intensify
items.summary: Subtropical western North Pacific typhoons crossing marine heatwaves had a 9-12% chance of rapid intensification about two days later, against 3.5-4.5% for storms that avoided them.

items.headline: UAlbany tests Google's AI cyclone model on four years of storms
items.meta: University at Albany · Geophysical Research Letters
items.summary: The study scored WeatherNext Cyclone intensity forecasts for every tropical cyclone from June 2022 to May 2026 against NHC and JTWC. The model may miss detail needed for the strongest, fastest-intensifying storms; the 2026 version was not tested.

items.headline: AuroraChem couples chemical and meteorological data assimilation in one model
items.summary: Researchers fine-tuned an atmospheric foundation model to include chemistry. Idealised tests show chemical observations constrain the meteorological state and vice versa, and the model's low cost makes ensemble assimilation practical.

items.headline: Review compares data-driven and NWP forecasts of extreme weather
items.summary: The review surveys how ML and physics-based models handle extremes and finds hybrid systems combining the two show some of the largest gains.

items.headline: Sparse autoencoder audit finds GraphCast relies on mesh-locked features
items.summary: Ablating a feature tied to GraphCast's computational mesh raised global geopotential height error even though the feature has no physical meaning. The authors argue physical interpretability and causal usefulness are separate properties.

items.headline: WeatherCraft cuts day-15 error with a token-based ensemble
items.summary: The framework encodes weather states as discrete tokens and aligns one model with reinforcement learning. On ERA5, an eight-member ensemble mean reduced day-15 normalized RMSE by 17.6% against the strongest deterministic baseline tested.

items.headline: Fengyun-4B rapid-scan winds improve 6 h typhoon intensity forecasts
items.summary: One-minute cloud-motion winds give upper-level vorticity within 100 km of the storm centre. Across 12 typhoons from 2022-2025, adding it to two statistical models reduced 6 h intensity errors on average.

items.headline: El Niño wind shift shuts down coastal upwelling off California
items.summary: Changed surface winds stopped the upwelling that keeps California's nearshore water cold, driving a marine heatwave. Zeke Hausfather says the El Niño is likely the strongest in 1,000 years based on tree-ring and coral records.

items.title: Tomorrow.io says its sounder data cut AI model start-state error by 5-8%
items.body_html: Tomorrow.io reported that adding its microwave-sounder data to its Sky 1 ML assimilation cut initial water-vapour error by about 5-8% across 28 cases scored against ERA5. It says Aurora 1.5 started from Sky 1 gained about a day of near-surface temperature lead time over GFS starts. Results are company-reported.

items.title: Xweather's Atmo launches a 14-day AI forecast for the Philippines with PAGASA
items.body_html: DOST and Atmo released the free Philippines AI Forecast, with 14-day forecasts updated every 15 minutes from PAGASA radar, station and satellite data. It is Atmo's first national deployment since Vaisala Xweather bought the company in October.

items.title: Meteomatics opens a weather drone base at McAlester airport in Oklahoma
items.body_html: Meteomatics will run its second operational Meteobase at McAlester Regional Airport, its first at an active US airport. It flies under the NOAA National Mesonet Program and feeds boundary-layer profiles into Meteomatics' US1k model.

items.title: StormGeo's Climatempo builds a three-radar network in Rio Grande do Sul
items.body_html: Climatempo will build and operate three S-band radars for the state government, with a data platform and monitoring services. Sites were picked from 32 candidates after the 2024 floods, adding to the Porto Alegre radar Climatempo already runs.

items.title: MITRE expands its weather modeling work with TempoQuest for federal missions
items.body_html: MITRE and TempoQuest broadened their partnership to apply GPU-accelerated forecasting to national security and wildfire missions, starting with porting MPAS to GPUs. TempoQuest's AceCAST helped build MITRE's Weather 1K dataset, which The Weather Company licensed in April.

items.title: ECMWF and partners win two HPCwire awards for AI forecasting
items.body_html: ECMWF and European met services won Best Use of HPC/AI in Physical Sciences for operational AI models, and Forecast-in-a-Box won the societal response category. Forecast-in-a-Box lets public institutions run AI forecasts on their own hardware, a free alternative to commercial on-premise products.

items.title: ECMWF details free forecast data for WMO members under Early Warnings for All
items.body_html: ECMWF set out its support for national met services, centred on the WMO Support Dataset. The free regional feed initialises limited-area models such as WRF and ICON, is for official use only and cannot be redistributed.

items.title: Metop-SG B1 launch slot set for no earlier than Dec 17
items.body_html: Orbital Radar lists the Ariane 6 launch of EUMETSAT's first Metop Second Generation B satellite from Kourou no earlier than Dec 17, a slot set on Nov 19. ESA said in October it expected launch at the end of the year.

items.title: Texas Tech starts a $24M mesonet and radar build in the Texas Hill Country
items.body_html: Texas Tech is using $24 million in state funds to add about 40 mesonet stations, three radars and a 48-hour high-resolution ensemble, with full deployment targeted for fall 2027. It is a public network in a region where private radar networks also operate.

items.title: SatSure raises $21M with investment from an Indian sovereign fund
items.body_html: Indian Earth observation analytics firm SatSure closed a $21 million Series B of equity, debt and secondaries, with India's sovereign space-tech fund investing. Its subsidiary KaleidEO has flight-tested an optical payload but has not yet launched a satellite.

items.title: SatLeo Labs holds $54M in letters of intent for thermal satellites
items.body_html: The Ahmedabad startup has raised about $6M since 2023 and plans satellites mapping land-surface temperature. It pitches near-real-time temperature data for heat, wildfire and crop monitoring.

items.title: constellr and Bulgarian Academy of Sciences plan a satellite crisis centre in Plovdiv
items.body_html: Thermal-imaging satellite firm constellr signed a cooperation agreement to build a centre monitoring wildfires, floods, farming and water use in southern Bulgaria. The partners plan to apply for EU funding.
